### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://www.stardima.com/tvshow/video-58/play/1445](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.stardima.com%2Ftvshow%2Fvideo-58%2Fplay%2F1445) ### Comment > #Bug Report: $popup Modifier Incorrectly Blocks XMLHttpRequest/HLS Requests > Affected Filters: Liste FR / Liste AR > Platforms: AdGuard for Android, AdGuard for Linux > Somehow Not Reproducible On: AdGuard for iOS (same configuration) > > ##Description > AdGuard is blocking XMLHttpRequest and media-file (HLS playlist) requests required for embedded video players to function. These requests are triggered by pages hosted on domains listed in the domain= option of $popup rules from the Liste FR and Liste AR filter lists. > > Standard ad-blocking behavior dictates that the $popup modifier should only block document navigations that open new tabs or windows. It should not apply to XHR or media requests loading content within the current page or iframe. > As mentioned by the Liste AR/Liste FR maintainer [here](https://github.com/easylist/listear/issues/46#issuecomment-5540724117) > > ##Affected Rules > 1. Liste FR > Rule: > > $popup,domain=111movies.com|...|luluvdo.com|...|streamtape.com|... > > > 2. Liste AR > (Previously reported) > Rule: > > $popup,third-party,domain=4yftwvrdz7.sbs|6sfkrspw4u.sbs|ak.sv|alkoora.live|animeiat.tv|arabveturk.com|hd7live.xyz|hyperwatching.com|iplayerhls.com|koora-stream.live|koora24.sbs|kora-api.top|kora-tv.vip|larhu.website|segavid.com|strema.top|topcinema.cam|turkvearab.com|yalla4shoot.live > > > ##Specific Case: Liste FR > Trigger Page: 'https://luluvdo.com' (Explicitly listed in the domain= option of the Liste FR rule). > Blocked Request: The page attempts to load an HLS playlist: > 'https://cdn1020.cdn-tnmr.org/hls2/01/04333/wnis4myylpit_h/master.m3u8?t=c8CR0UQKCux6w592zgPk0jJxPD2bVIhlO5goClqYIk0&s=1789882305&e=28800&f=21665630&i=0.3&sp=0' > > Result: AdGuard blocks this request as a "popup," causing the video player to fail. > Mechanism: The rule is active because the page originates from luluvdo.com. However, the blocked request is an internal XHR/media fetch, not a new window navigation. > > ##Steps to Reproduce > 1. Enable EasyList, Liste FR, and Liste AR in AdGuard. > 2. Navigate to 'https://www.stardima.com/tvshow/video-58/play/1445'. > 3. Attempt to play an embedded video. > 4. Click on Lulustream (video server) > 5. Result: The video player fails to load. > > ##Workaround > Disabling Liste FR or Liste AR or whitelisting the specific domain allows the video to load. > > ##Observations > Comparison with Adblock Plus: Using the exact same filter lists in Adblock Plus does not block these requests. The video loads successfully. This indicates the filter syntax is valid and the issue lies in AdGuard's enforcement of the $popup modifier. > Maintainer Update: The maintainer of Liste AR revised their list after a similar report; the Liste AR rule no longer triggers this block, but the equivalent Liste FR rule continues to do so under the same conditions. > Platform Difference: The behavior is consistent on Android and Linux but absent on iOS. > Evidence > The following GitHub [comment](github.com/easylist/listear/issues/46#issuecomment-5550885943) in Liste AR confirms this issue and includes video recordings: > > > For more info please refer to issues [47](https://github.com/easylist/listear/issues/47) and [46](https://github.com/easylist/listear/issues/46) in Liste AR > ``` Username: @itskrona ``` ### Screenshots

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Ads)
[NSFW] [https://www.imdb.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.imdb.com%2F)

### Comment
> I've isolated a bug where domains confirmed as blocked by my active filter lists are still resolving live and serving content through my account's DNS servers. I've ruled out every variable on my end and would appreciate help checking server-side.
> 
> **Account/servers affected:**
> - DNS addresses: `94.140.14.49` / `94.140.14.59` (IPv4), `2a10:50c0::ded:ff` / `2a10:50c0::dad:ff` (IPv6)
> - Device profile: TP-Link Deco M5
> 
> **The issue:**
> `doubleclick.net` and `m.doubleclick.net` both show as **blocked** in your own "Check a domain" tool for this device:
> - `doubleclick.net` → blocked by **AdGuard DNS filter**, rule `||doubleclick.net^`
> - `m.doubleclick.net` → blocked by **OISD Blocklist Big**, rule `||m.doubleclick.net^`
> 
> But live queries to your resolvers return real answers for both, not a block:
> 
> ```
> nslookup doubleclick.net 94.140.14.49
> Server:  94-140-14-49.adguard-dns.com
> Address:  94.140.14.49
> 
> Non-authoritative answer:
> Name:    doubleclick.net
> Addresses:  2607:f8b0:4007:806::200e
>             142.251.41.14
> ```
> 
> **Live example — ad served from a blocked domain:**
> While browsing imdb.com, a banner ad loaded successfully via a request to `ad.doubleclick.net`, captured in my browser's Network tab:
> ```
> https://ad.doubleclick.net/ddm/adj/N805.2646AMAZONMEDIAGROUPLLC./B34608755.433941313;dc_ver=107.317;...
> ```
> Status: **200** (completed successfully)
> 
> This confirms the mismatch isn't limited to isolated `nslookup` testing — the domain is actively resolving and serving ad content in real browsing sessions despite being confirmed blocked.
> 
> **What I've ruled out:**
> - Local DNS cache — flushed repeatedly, no change
> - My own custom User Rules — tested with the toggle both on and off, no difference
> - My whitelist/custom filtering rules — checked for any rule referencing "doubleclick," none found
> - My router (TP-Link Deco M5, HomeShield security features disabled) and my ISP gateway (AT&T, IP Passthrough mode, Firewall Advanced settings all off) — ruled out by tethering a laptop to cellular data and querying `94.140.14.49` directly by IP, bypassing all home network equipment entirely. Same result: not blocked.
> - The Query Log shows no entry — blocked or otherwise — for queries to the bare `doubleclick.net` domain, even though live queries clearly reached your server and got an answer.
> 
> I would appreciate help figuring out why these ads are still not being blocked. 
> 
> Thanks,
> Josh

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Ads)
[NSFW] [https://www.imdb.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.imdb.com%2F)

### Comment
> I've isolated a bug where domains confirmed as blocked by my active filter lists are still resolving live and serving content through my account's DNS servers. I've ruled out every variable on my end and would appreciate help checking server-side.
> 
> **Account/servers affected:**
> - DNS addresses: `94.140.14.49` / `94.140.14.59` (IPv4), `2a10:50c0::ded:ff` / `2a10:50c0::dad:ff` (IPv6)
> - Device profile: TP-Link Deco M5
> 
> **The issue:**
> `doubleclick.net` and `m.doubleclick.net` both show as **blocked** in your own "Check a domain" tool for this device:
> - `doubleclick.net` → blocked by **AdGuard DNS filter**, rule `||doubleclick.net^`
> - `m.doubleclick.net` → blocked by **OISD Blocklist Big**, rule `||m.doubleclick.net^`
> 
> But live queries to your resolvers return real answers for both, not a block:
> 
> ```
> nslookup doubleclick.net 94.140.14.49
> Server:  94-140-14-49.adguard-dns.com
> Address:  94.140.14.49
> 
> Non-authoritative answer:
> Name:    doubleclick.net
> Addresses:  2607:f8b0:4007:806::200e
>             142.251.41.14
> ```
> 
> **Live example — ad served from a blocked domain:**
> While browsing imdb.com, a banner ad loaded successfully via a request to `ad.doubleclick.net`, captured in my browser's Network tab:
> ```
> https://ad.doubleclick.net/ddm/adj/N805.2646AMAZONMEDIAGROUPLLC./B34608755.433941313;dc_ver=107.317;...
> ```
> Status: **200** (completed successfully)
> 
> This confirms the mismatch isn't limited to isolated `nslookup` testing — the domain is actively resolving and serving ad content in real browsing sessions despite being confirmed blocked.
> 
> **What I've ruled out:**
> - Local DNS cache — flushed repeatedly, no change
> - My own custom User Rules — tested with the toggle both on and off, no difference
> - My whitelist/custom filtering rules — checked for any rule referencing "doubleclick," none found
> - My router (TP-Link Deco M5, HomeShield security features disabled) and my ISP gateway (AT&T, IP Passthrough mode, Firewall Advanced settings all off) — ruled out by tethering a laptop to cellular data and querying `94.140.14.49` directly by IP, bypassing all home network equipment entirely. Same result: not blocked.
> - The Query Log shows no entry — blocked or otherwise — for queries to the bare `doubleclick.net` domain, even though live queries clearly reached your server and got an answer.
> 
> I would appreciate help figuring out why these ads are still not being blocked. 
> 
> Thanks,
> Josh

### Issue URL (Ads) [https://kaliscan.com/home](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fkaliscan.com%2Fhome) ### Comment > On the Kaliscan website (a large manga aggregation site), as of today, they have installed a new form of overlay that appears only after scrolling for a short time. It is typically a fake login screen or fake capcha that when clicked (even clicking the X) automatically opens a new tab with a redirect to an inappropriate site. > > Notably, when trying to use the element blocker, the AdGuard modal appears _below_ the fake login/capcha, meaning it is quite literally impossible to block via normal means. Even when you open the ‘block element’ mode and wait, clicking on the element just triggers the redirect rather than selecting it to be blocked. The redirect itself typically gives a ‘site blocked’ page, but it is very annoying. > > Notably this morning there was a bunch of error codes at the top of the page, presumably when the site owner installed the cancerous software and was setting it up. Если вы используете расширение AdGuard для браузера, рекомендуется также установить AdGuard Extra.

issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS. 


Previous issue https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/198973

# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS. 


Previous issue https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/198973

It is a religious/educational site with no adult content, so this looks like a **false positive**, or possibly a resolution failure on a regional server. > > ### Environment > | | | > |---|---| > | **Device** | Samsung Android phone | > | **DNS setup** | Android Private DNS (DNS-over-TLS) → `family.adguard-dns.com` | > | **Location** | Brazil | > | **Date observed** | 2026-09-24 | > > ### Steps to reproduce > 1. Set Android Private DNS to `family.adguard-dns.com` > 2. Open `https://www.jw.org` in any browser > > ### Expected behavior > The site loads normally. > > ### Actual behavior > The browser shows **"Address Not Found"** because the hostname does not resolve. > > - ❌ Fails in **Firefox** and **Chrome** > - ❌ Fails on **Wi-Fi** and **mobile data** > - ✅ Works immediately when Private DNS is turned **off** > > ### Affected domains > - `jw.org` > - `www.jw.org` > - `wol.jw.org` > > ### Request > Please check whether `jw.org` is on a Family Protection / parental-control list, or whether DoT queries for these domains are failing, and unblock or fix them if so. ``` Username: @mattbbia ``` ### Screenshots

It is a religious/educational site with no adult content, so this looks like a **false positive**, or possibly a resolution failure on a regional server. > > ### Environment > | | | > |---|---| > | **Device** | Samsung Android phone | > | **DNS setup** | Android Private DNS (DNS-over-TLS) → `family.adguard-dns.com` | > | **Location** | Brazil | > | **Date observed** | 2026-09-24 | > > ### Steps to reproduce > 1. Set Android Private DNS to `family.adguard-dns.com` > 2. Open `https://www.jw.org` in any browser > > ### Expected behavior > The site loads normally. > > ### Actual behavior > The browser shows **"Address Not Found"** because the hostname does not resolve. > > - ❌ Fails in **Firefox** and **Chrome** > - ❌ Fails on **Wi-Fi** and **mobile data** > - ✅ Works immediately when Private DNS is turned **off** > > ### Affected domains > - `jw.org` > - `www.jw.org` > - `wol.jw.org` > > ### Request > Please check whether `jw.org` is on a Family Protection / parental-control list, or whether DoT queries for these domains are failing, and unblock or fix them if so. ``` Username: @mattbbia ``` ### Screenshots

issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS.

### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://store.steampowered.com/app/1621690/Core_Keeper/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.steampowered.com%2Fapp%2F1621690%2FCore_Keeper%2F) ### Comment > Core Keeper multiplayer connection is lost when AdGuard for Windows is enabled and the SockFilter network driver is being used. > > Core Keeper works normally in single-player mode. However, when I try to play multiplayer, the game displays the following error: > > "Connection to the multiplayer backend was lost. > To re-enable multiplayer, exit and reopen the game world." > > The problem occurs even though I have added Core Keeper.exe to AdGuard's filtering exclusions. > > I tested the following: > > - AdGuard enabled + SockFilter: multiplayer connection is lost. > - AdGuard disabled: multiplayer works normally. > - Core Keeper.exe added to AdGuard's filtering exclusions: the problem still occurs. > - The problem only affects multiplayer; single-player gameplay works normally. > > I also tested the WFP network driver. issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS. 


Previous issue https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/198973

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Ads)
[NSFW] [https://www.imdb.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.imdb.com%2F)

### Comment
> I've isolated a bug where domains confirmed as blocked by my active filter lists are still resolving live and serving content through my account's DNS servers. I've ruled out every variable on my end and would appreciate help checking server-side.
> 
> **Account/servers affected:**
> - DNS addresses: `94.140.14.49` / `94.140.14.59` (IPv4), `2a10:50c0::ded:ff` / `2a10:50c0::dad:ff` (IPv6)
> - Device profile: TP-Link Deco M5
> 
> **The issue:**
> `doubleclick.net` and `m.doubleclick.net` both show as **blocked** in your own "Check a domain" tool for this device:
> - `doubleclick.net` → blocked by **AdGuard DNS filter**, rule `||doubleclick.net^`
> - `m.doubleclick.net` → blocked by **OISD Blocklist Big**, rule `||m.doubleclick.net^`
> 
> But live queries to your resolvers return real answers for both, not a block:
> 
> ```
> nslookup doubleclick.net 94.140.14.49
> Server:  94-140-14-49.adguard-dns.com
> Address:  94.140.14.49
> 
> Non-authoritative answer:
> Name:    doubleclick.net
> Addresses:  2607:f8b0:4007:806::200e
>             142.251.41.14
> ```
> 
> **Live example — ad served from a blocked domain:**
> While browsing imdb.com, a banner ad loaded successfully via a request to `ad.doubleclick.net`, captured in my browser's Network tab:
> ```
> https://ad.doubleclick.net/ddm/adj/N805.2646AMAZONMEDIAGROUPLLC./B34608755.433941313;dc_ver=107.317;...
> ```
> Status: **200** (completed successfully)
> 
> This confirms the mismatch isn't limited to isolated `nslookup` testing — the domain is actively resolving and serving ad content in real browsing sessions despite being confirmed blocked.
> 
> **What I've ruled out:**
> - Local DNS cache — flushed repeatedly, no change
> - My own custom User Rules — tested with the toggle both on and off, no difference
> - My whitelist/custom filtering rules — checked for any rule referencing "doubleclick," none found
> - My router (TP-Link Deco M5, HomeShield security features disabled) and my ISP gateway (AT&T, IP Passthrough mode, Firewall Advanced settings all off) — ruled out by tethering a laptop to cellular data and querying `94.140.14.49` directly by IP, bypassing all home network equipment entirely. Same result: not blocked.
> - The Query Log shows no entry — blocked or otherwise — for queries to the bare `doubleclick.net` domain, even though live queries clearly reached your server and got an answer.
> 
> I would appreciate help figuring out why these ads are still not being blocked. 
> 
> Thanks,
> Josh

```
Username: @joshkaspar
```

However, when I try to play multiplayer, the game displays the following error: > > "Connection to the multiplayer backend was lost. > To re-enable multiplayer, exit and reopen the game world." > > The problem occurs even though I have added Core Keeper.exe to AdGuard's filtering exclusions. > > I tested the following: > > - AdGuard enabled + SockFilter: multiplayer connection is lost. > - AdGuard disabled: multiplayer works normally. > - Core Keeper.exe added to AdGuard's filtering exclusions: the problem still occurs. > - The problem only affects multiplayer; single-player gameplay works normally. > > I also tested the WFP network driver. issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS. 


Previous issue https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/198973
